subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a militarized hover pickup design: no wheels, hover thruster pods at the four corners, an armored cab, a roof turret, and a rocket pod in the bed, all with neon glow accents and decal textures, keeping the module compact enough to run cleanly without errors.

I'm working out the chassis as a skeleton with a root joint, turret yaw/pitch joints, and spinning thruster fans, sizing the truck at roughly 5.5 by 2.1 units with the hover pods and landing skids resting at floor level so it still touches down naturally. For materials I'm defining a gunmetal body paint with dirt wear and edge highlighting, plus magenta and cyan neon glow accents, alongside hazard-stripe and decal textures built from SVG.

For geometry I'm laying out the hull as a belly box with skid rails underneath, then adding ducted-fan thruster pods on struts at each corner with cyan emissive under-glow discs and spinning fan blades inside their shrouds.

Working out the fan blades now: seven thin boxes arranged radially around a joint, each rotated by angle around the Y axis so its long axis points outward from the pod's center.

Adding a glow disc beneath the pod...

Now I'm designing the cab geometry: a boxy militarized structure with a lower armored body, slanted greenhouse windscreen with teal tint, flat roof, pillars, and a sloped frustum hood up front. I'm adding armor plates, narrow slit windows, door seams, a hazard stripe decal on the hood, and a number decal on the door using a textured plane.

For the truck bed I'm placing the floor and walls, a rocket pod with tube racks, a glowing fusion core, and a roll bar, then adding a roof turret with yaw/pitch joints for twin autocannons and a magenta lightbar, plus a front ram bumper with spikes, glowing cyan headlight slits, a grille intake, and rear magenta tail lights with a thruster.

Now I'm adding the dual rear thruster nozzles shaped like bells with glow, neon cyan underglow strips along the side skirts, and a "NOMAD" neon sign rendered as SVG text with a glowing backing plate on the bed instead of trying CJK glyphs. I'm settling on the full texture set: hazard stripes, the "07" number plate, the neon sign, a skull-like emblem, a radar screen, a warning label, and gradient glass reflections.

I'm defining a procedural body paint function that mixes wear colors using noise, darkens seams and crevices, adds dusty tinting near the ground, and brightens upward-facing surfaces slightly for a metallic sheen -- plus thinking through how to fake panel seam lines using periodic z-position patterns.

Now I'm planning an armor plate accent material with a cyberpunk feel: a darker scratched base color with a thin magenta stripe band placed along a specific height range on side-facing surfaces of the body.

Setting up geometry helpers and starting to build the hover truck structure, defining a chassis joint and a reusable part-creation function...

Now I'm working out cab dimensions layer by layer—lower body box, upper cab box, roof plate, and a raked windscreen plane—using mirrored side loops for symmetry.

For the windscreen I'm tilting a thin glass box backward about the X axis so the top edge slopes rearward like a real cab, giving it a dark teal glass color. I'm adding narrow armored side windows near the A-pillars, plus pillar rods for structure.

Now I'm shaping the hood as a frustum wedge narrowing toward the front, checking the slope heights match where the windscreen base sits, and adding an armor plate on top of the hood with hazard-stripe texturing oriented upward.

Next I'm detailing the nose: a dark grille box with glowing cyan slats, slit headlights glowing near the edges, and a ram-style bumper with spike teeth and a tow ring, all in the dark body color scheme.

Then I'm adding camera-pod mirrors, door seams with handles, a license plate decal, and placing the emblem on the tailgate or lower door area.

For the bed, I'm laying out a floor box roughly centered behind the cab, with side walls, a headboard, and a tailgate sized to fit the bed's length and height.

I'm checking that the hull belly extends under the bed and cab without clipping, adjusting its vertical position so it sits just below the cab floor, then repositioning the wheel-arch pods outward on the x-axis so they clear the hull's width.

Now I'm adding struts connecting the hull sides to the pods, plus wing stubs, and placing bed items: a glowing fusion-core cylinder with a cyan glass tube, and a rocket launcher pod on the bed with angled tube clusters facing forward.

Adding the sign glow onto the headboard's rear face, then setting up the turret with yaw and pitch joints on the cab roof, and detailing the turret components: a base ring torus, drum cylinder, cheeks, twin barrel rods with glowing muzzles, an ammo box, and a magenta sensor eye.

Still placing details... roof rack lightbar and antenna, rear thruster nozzles with cyan glow discs, taillight strips, tailgate emblem, underglow strips along the hull sides, and skid rods with support struts beneath the body.

Actually skids already handle ground contact, so pods hover naturally at 0.25 once landed — that simplifies things. Now I'm sketching the texture assets: a hazard stripe pattern for warning panels and a numbered plate texture with glowing pink digits on a dark background.

Next I'm designing the remaining decals — a neon sign panel, a hex-shaped skull emblem, a radar screen display, and a high-voltage warning triangle, all using monospace text in cyan and magenta. I'm also settling on the final color palette for body paint, armor, dark steel, gunmetal, cyan, magenta, and amber accents.

I'm working out a plane-decal helper that attaches texture planes to the chassis bone with a configurable facing direction and "up" orientation so the artwork reads correctly from the front, then placing a number plate decal on the door with its own glow effect.

I'll apply the glow effect selectively—to the number plate, sign, and screen decals, while leaving hazard/warning/emblem elements unglowed (or possibly glowing the emblem too). For the cab sides, I'm positioning decals just outside the chassis box width, adding a body paint stripe, and building armor plates on the doors as boxes with bolts added via a small loop.

Still writing bolt and turret structure...

Still building spikes and cables...
